name: symbolic_calculus
title: Symbolic Calculus
summary: Exact symbolic differentiation and integration of a single expression provided as a string, returning SymPy expression strings.

tools.name: differentiate
tools.description: Compute the nth derivative of a symbolic expression with respect to one variable.

params.name: expression
params.description: The expression to differentiate, in SymPy/Python syntax.

params.name: variable
params.description: The differentiation variable, such as x.

params.name: order
params.description: The derivative order. Defaults to 1; 0 returns the original expression.

returns.name: derivative
returns.description: The resulting derivative as a SymPy expression string.

tools.implementation_notes: Import sympify from sympy (or sympy.core.sympify) and diff from sympy (or sympy.core.function). Convert expression and variable with sympify(...). Default order to 1, then call diff(expr, var, order); this is equivalent to expr.diff(var, order) and supports order 0. Return str(result) as derivative, echoing the original expression, variable, and order.

tools.name: integrate
tools.description: Compute the indefinite or definite integral of a symbolic expression with respect to one variable.

params.name: variable
params.description: The integration variable, such as x.

params.name: lower_limit
params.description: Optional lower limit for definite integration. Provide together with upper_limit; may be numeric or symbolic, such as 0 or pi.

params.name: upper_limit
params.description: Optional upper limit for definite integration. Provide together with lower_limit; may be numeric or symbolic, such as 1 or oo.

returns.name: definite
returns.description: Whether a definite integral was computed.

returns.name: limits
returns.description: For definite integrals, [lower_limit, upper_limit] as strings; otherwise an empty array.

returns.name: integral
returns.description: The resulting integral as a SymPy expression string. An unevaluated Integral(...) string is returned when SymPy cannot evaluate it.

returns.name: evaluated
returns.description: Whether SymPy returned an evaluated expression rather than an unevaluated Integral object.

tools.implementation_notes: Import sympify from sympy (or sympy.core.sympify) and integrate from sympy (or sympy.integrals.integrals). Convert expression and variable with sympify(...). If both lower_limit and upper_limit are provided, convert each with sympify(...) and call integrate(expr, (var, lower, upper)); otherwise call integrate(expr, var). Require both limits or neither, raising ValueError if only one is provided. Set definite true only when both limits are provided, and limits to [str(lower_limit), str(upper_limit)] or []. Return str(result) as integral. Set evaluated by checking that result is not an instance of sympy.integrals.integrals.Integral.

uncertainties: Expression and variable strings are parsed with sympy.sympify; invalid syntax raises SympifyError.
The derivative order must be a non-negative integer; sympy.diff semantics apply, including order 0 returning the original expression.
Definite integration requires both lower_limit and upper_limit; providing only one should raise ValueError.
Limits may be numeric or symbolic strings such as 0, pi, or oo and are sympified before integration.
If SymPy cannot evaluate an integral, integrate returns an unevaluated Integral object whose string representation is returned.
Indefinite integrals omit the arbitrary constant of integration.
